<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Sp1nd01" /></noinclude>to paſſe ouer the earth, and the waters aſſwaged.

{{Verse|8|2}} The fountaines alſo of the deepe, and the windowes of heauen were ſtopped, and the raine from heauen was reſtrained.

{{Verse|8|3}} And the waters returned from off the earth, †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr.'' in ''going and returning.''}} continually: and after the end of the hundred and fiftie dayes, the waters were abated.

{{Verse|8|4}} And the Arke reſted in the ſeuenth moneth, on the ſeuenteenth day of the moneth, vpon the mountaines of Ararat.

{{Verse|8|5}} And the waters †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr.'' were ''in going and decreaſing.''}} decreaſed continually vntill the tenth moneth: in the tenth moneth, on the firſt {{smaller|day}} of the moneth, were the tops of the mountaines ſeen.

{{Verse|8|6}} ¶And it came to paſſe at the end of the forty dayes, that Noah opened the window of the Arke which he had made.

{{Verse|8|7}} And he ſent forth a Rauen, which went foorth †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr.'' in ''going foorth, and returning.''}} to and fro, vntill the waters were dried vp from off the earth.

{{Verse|8|8}} Alſo hee ſent foorth a doue from him, to ſee if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground.

{{Verse|8|9}} But the doue found no reſt for the ſole of her foote, and ſhe returned vnto him into the Arke: for the waters {{smaller|were}} on the face of the whole earth. Then he put foorth his hand, and tooke her, and †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. cauſed her to come.''}} pulled her in vnto him, into the Arke.

{{Verse|8|10}} And hee ſtayed yet other ſeuen dayes; and againe hee ſent foorth the doue out of the Arke.

{{Verse|8|11}} And the doue came in to him in the euening, and loe, in her mouth {{smaller|was}} an Oliue leafe pluckt off: So Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.

{{Verse|8|12}} And hee ſtayed yet other ſeuen dayes, and ſent forth the doue, which returned not againe vnto him any more.

{{Verse|8|13}} ¶And it came to paſſe in the ſixe hundredth and one yeere, in the firſt {{smaller|moneth}}, the firſt {{smaller|day}} of the moneth, the waters were dryed vp from {{smaller|off}} the earth: and Noah remooued the couering of the Arke, and looked, and behold, the face of the ground was drie.

{{Verse|8|14}} And in the ſecond moneth, on the ſeuen and twentieth day of the moneth, was the earth dried.

{{Verse|8|15}} ¶And God spake vnto Noah, ſaying,

{{Verse|8|16}} Goe foorth of the Arke, thou, and thy wife, and thy ſonnes, and thy ſonnes wiues with thee:

{{Verse|8|17}} Bring foorth with thee euery liuing thing that {{smaller|is}} with thee, of all fleſh, {{smaller|both}} of fowle, and of cattell, and of euery creeping thing that creepeth vpon the earth, that they may breed abundantly in the earth, and be fruitfull, and multiply vpon the earth.

{{Verse|8|18}} And Noah went foorth, and his ſonnes, and his wife, and his ſonnes wiues with him:

{{Verse|8|19}} Euery beaſt, euery creeping thing, and euery fowle, {{smaller|and}} whatſoeuer creepeth vpon the earth, after their †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. families.''}} kinds, went foorth out of the Arke.

{{Verse|8|20}} ¶And Noah builded an Altar vnto the LORD, and tooke of euery cleane beaſt, and of euery cleane fowle, and offred burnt offrings on the Altar.

{{Verse|8|21}} And the LORD ſmelled a †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. a ſouour of reſt.''}} ſweete ſauour, and the LORD ſaid in his heart, I will not againe curſe the ground any more for mans ſake; for the *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Chapt.6.5. matt.15.19.}} imagination of mans heart {{smaller|is}} euil from his youth: neither will I againe ſmite any more euery thing liuing, as I haue done.

{{Verse|8|22}} †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. as yet all the dayes of the earth''}} While the earth remaineth, ſeed-time and harueſt, and cold, and heat, and Summer, and Winter, and day and night, ſhall not ceaſe.

{{c|{{Chapter|9|CHAP. IX.}}}}

{{smaller block|[[#9:1|1]] God bleſſeth Noah. [[#9:4|4]] Blood and murder are forbidden. [[#9:9|9]] Gods Couenant [[#9:13|13]] ſignified by the Rainebow. [[#9:18|18]] Noah repleniſheth the world, [[#9:20|20]] planteth a Vineyard, [[#9:21|21]] is drunken, and mocked of his ſonne: [[#9:25|25]] Curſeth Canaan, [[#9:26|26]] Bleſſeth Shem, [[#9:27|27]] Prayeth for Iaphet, [[#9:28|28]] and dieth.}}

{{Verse|9|1|notext=}} 
{{dropinitial|A|image=King James Bible (1611) page A3v (A).png|imgsize=100px}}Nd God bleſſed Noah, and his ſonnes, and ſaid vnto them, *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Chapt.1.28. and 8.17.}} Bee fruitfull and multiply, and repleniſh the earth.

{{Verse|9|2}} And the feare of you, ⁊ the dread of you ſhall be vpon euery beaſt of the earth, and vpon euery fowle of the aire, vpon all that mooueth {{smaller|vpon}} the earth, and vpon all the fiſhes of the ſea; into your hand are they deliuered.

{{Verse|9|3}} Euery mouing thing that liueth, ſhal be meat for you; euen as the *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Chapt.1.29.}} greene herbe haue I giuen you all things.

{{Verse|9|4}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Leuit.17.14.}} But fleſh with the life thereof, {{smaller|which is}} the blood thereof, ſhall you not eate.

{{Verse|9|5}} And ſurely your blood of your<noinclude></noinclude>
